title: Insertion sort respects its comparison recurrence
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $xs$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$. Running the timed insertion sort on $xs$ charges at most $T(\abs{xs})$ units of time, where $\abs{xs}$ is the length of $xs$ and $T$ is the recurrence given by $T(0) = 0$ and $T(n+1) = T(n) + n$.
replaced:
The time cost recorded by the timed insertion sort of $\mathit{xs}$ is at most
$T(\abs{\mathit{xs}})$, where $T$ is the insertion sort recurrence.
